eyebrow: CHARITY RESEARCH · UNITED STATES · EARLY CHILDHOOD HEALTH
program: National Nurse-Family Partnership implementation support, with Child First in the same legal organization

nutshell.headline: Legacy mortality evidence is promising, but a modern RCT's age-two primary composite was null and marginal gift leverage is unverified.
nutshell.body: A $100,000 ordinary-gift model yields 0.06621 signed QALY, or $15.10 million donor cost and $22.01 million gross-resource cost per 10 modeled QALYs. Central is $14.97 million/$26.47 million. A 5%-weight favorable case supplies 85.23% of the signed expectation; without it, donor cost worsens to $97.12 million per 10 QALYs. These are conditional priors, not a marginal offer.
nutshell.whyItMayWork: Nurse-Family Partnership is unusually well studied. A Memphis randomized-trial follow-up found nine preventable-cause deaths in the comparison group and none in the pregnancy-plus-infancy nurse-visited group through age 20.
nutshell.whyWeAreCautious: A 5,670-person modern South Carolina RCT found a null age-two primary composite. Changent supports local implementers rather than directly employing San Francisco nurses, the legal entity also operates Child First, and no priced next-gift expansion plan or local funding gap was found.
nutshell.recommendationBlocker: Obtain unrestricted-gift allocation across NFP, Child First, policy, and reserves; SF unique active, new, and completing families; unserved eligible referrals; marginal national-office and local delivery costs; cofunding; fidelity; and a preregistered local outcome plan.

programSection.body: Changent is the national umbrella for Nurse-Family Partnership and Child First. For NFP, local implementing partners employ nurses while Changent supplies education, infrastructure, monitoring, support, and network development. NFP begins during pregnancy and continues until the child turns two.

steps.title: Enroll during pregnancy
steps.detail: Eligible first-time mothers are connected to a trained nurse through a local implementing partner; Changent is the national support organization rather than the direct SF employer.

steps.title: Visit through age two
steps.detail: Nurses provide a roughly 2.5-year pregnancy-to-age-two course focused on maternal health, child health and development, and family economic self-sufficiency.

steps.title: Support the delivery network
steps.detail: Changent trains and supports local partners, monitors implementation, operates shared infrastructure, and also houses Child First. An ordinary Changent gift is not represented as restricted to NFP or San Francisco.

programSection.boundary: The full $30,712,013 FY2024 Changent expense is charged while Child First and other non-NFP activity receive zero modeled QALYs. Changent reported 57,005 NFP families served in 2024, an annual active-family count rather than starts, exposure-years, retention, or completed courses. The model first computes $538.759986 per active-family-year and divides active-family units by the official 2.5-year course span, producing $1,346.899965 Changent expense per modeled full-course equivalent. This is a unit-alignment approximation, not an observed completion denominator or marginal family price.

model.headline: Prior-weighted modeled ordinary gift: $15.10M per 10 QALYs; central: $14.97M.
model.body: The signed model aligns annual active-family units to full 2.5-year courses before applying full-course QALYs and delivery costs. It charges outside implementation resources to funded course-equivalents before the separate realization factor, while QALYs accrue only to realized courses. It charges all Changent expense, assigns Child First and unmodeled activities zero benefit, includes harm and null cases, and treats Bay/SF allocation as constant national-gift priors.

equation.label: CENTRAL MODELED GIFT COST
equation.expression: 10 × $100,000 ÷ [($10,000 additional support ÷ $538.759986 active-family-year cost ÷ 2.5 years × 90% realization) × 0.010 QALY/full course]
equation.result: $14,965,555 per 10 modeled QALYs; 6.682011 realized full-course equivalents and 0.0668201 gift-attributed QALY

model.inputColumnLabel: Harm / null / cautious / central / favorable judgments

inputs.label: Whole-organization cost and annual active-family denominator
inputs.confidence: High accounting; moderate organization output; low course-equivalence precision
inputs.basis: All Changent expense is charged; 2,564 Child First families and other activities receive zero QALYs. Reported families are annual active units, not new enrollments or completions.

inputs.label: Modeled full-course duration
inputs.confidence: High program design; low retention/completion observation
inputs.basis: Official NFP care runs from pregnancy until the child turns two. Dividing annual active-family units by 2.5 aligns benefit and cost units but is not measured retention or completion.

inputs.label: Scenario prior weights
inputs.basis: The modern primary-composite result was null, the legacy mortality signal is sparse and non-prespecified, and marginal gift leverage is unverified; null plus harm therefore receive 50% weight.

inputs.label: Ordinary-gift funding additionality
inputs.basis: Share of the gift assumed to cause support for an otherwise-unserved family rather than reserves, fee/grant substitution, or planned activity. Changent publishes no priced expansion offer or bottleneck.

inputs.label: Course realization
inputs.basis: Discounts modeled course-equivalents for incomplete exposure, retention, fidelity, and implementation failure; it is not a measured completion rate.

inputs.label: QALY per realized full course
inputs.basis: Memphis calibration is 0.016 preventable-death risk difference × a 9-QALY undiscounted within-age-20 cap = 0.144 QALY/full course. Scenario credits are judgmental fractions, not trial QALY estimates.

inputs.label: Finite mortality calibration
inputs.basis: Assumes approximately ten undiscounted remaining years within the observed age-20 window at 0.9 utility and gives no survival credit after age 20.

inputs.label: Full delivery cost per funded course-equivalent
inputs.confidence: Moderate historical evidence; low current-SF transfer
inputs.basis: Historical 2012 national present-value and 2019 California estimates. For each pre-realization funded course-equivalent, the model subtracts the aligned $1,346.90 Changent amount before adding outside implementation resources; QALYs still accrue only after realization. This may overstate partner cost for early exits, but avoids treating incomplete or failed realization as consuming zero outside resources. These are not current SF marginal prices.

inputs.label: Bay and San Francisco impact shares
inputs.basis: Bay means the nine-county region and SF is nested. The priors combine a mismatched 5,811 California-capacity/57,005 national-family proxy with unsourced round 25%-of-California Bay and 2%-of-California SF splits; proportional national-gift allocation is also assumed.

sensitivity.headline: −0.011879 modeled QALY
sensitivity.detail: 1.187913 modeled full courses at −0.010 QALY/course; no positive donor or gross ratio.

sensitivity.headline: No modeled QALYs
sensitivity.detail: 1.781870 modeled full courses but zero QALY/course; donor and gross ratios are not defined.

sensitivity.headline: $15.10M modeled donor cost per 10 QALYs
sensitivity.detail: 0.066208 expected QALY and $22.01M gross-resource cost. Favorable contributes 85.23% of signed expected QALYs; without it, donor cost is $97.12M.

model.uncertaintyBoundary: Funding additionality, realization, QALY transfer, harm, geography, and scenario weights are analyst priors, not confidence intervals or measured Changent effects. The age-two primary composite was null; the age-20 mortality signal was sparse and not prespecified. Zero funding additionality returns zero QALYs and null donor, gross, Bay, and SF ratios.
model.fundingBoundary: Health-producing marginal RFMF is unverified and appears constrained. Changent accepts ordinary gifts to EIN 20-0234163, but does not promise NFP- or SF-restriction or publish a next-$100,000 family target, local cofunding gap, waitlist, or binding national-office constraint. FY2024 total net assets of $111.212M were 3.6 times expense, but are not demonstrated liquid or unrestricted; pledge restrictions, timing, and liquidity are unavailable.

evidence.population: Memphis pregnancy-plus-infancy nurse-visited and comparison families; 690 surviving children in the mortality analysis
evidence.result: Nine preventable-cause deaths occurred in the comparison group and none in the nurse-visited group; estimated preventable mortality was 1.6% versus 0 through age 20 (P=.04). All-cause mortality was 2.7% versus 0.9% (P=.11).
evidence.transfer: Mortality was not prespecified and events were sparse. The model uses a finite 0.144-QALY/full-course calibration only as a ceiling and credits −0.010 to 0.080 QALY/course across scenarios.

evidence.population: 5,670 Medicaid-eligible pregnant people across nine implementing authorities; 4,932 live births in child analysis
evidence.result: The age-two primary composite was 27.3% with NFP versus 26.8% with usual care, adjusted +0.4 percentage points (95% CI −2.3 to 3.0). ED use fell 2.9 points but lost significance after multiplicity adjustment.
evidence.transfer: Strong counterevidence for the contemporary age-two primary composite, but it does not resolve later outcomes. The model gives null plus harm 50% weight rather than pooling incompatible endpoints.

evidence.result: Estimated $8,580 present-value full cost per family in 2012 prices.
evidence.transfer: Historical full-delivery proxy, not a current SF marginal quote; used only for the favorable gross-resource case.

evidence.design: California NFP impact and cost profile
evidence.transfer: Historical California proxy used in harm/null/cautious gross-resource cases; does not establish current local resources or marginal capacity.

evidence.population: National 2024 NFP and Child First activity
evidence.result: 57,005 NFP families, 586,081 visits, 2,100 NFP nurses/supervisors, and 2,564 Child First families.
evidence.transfer: No counterfactual and no observed start/completion cohort. Annual active-family units are divided by 2.5 before applying full-course effects and costs.

evidence.result: Revenue $42.540M, expense $30.712M, surplus $11.828M, total net assets $111.212M, contributions $21.451M, and program-service revenue $17.026M.
evidence.transfer: Full expense remains in the denominator. Total net assets are not proven liquid or unrestricted and do not establish a health-producing marginal gift opportunity.

reservations: The receiving legal organization includes Child First and non-NFP activity; all expense is charged while those pathways receive zero QALYs.
Reported families served are annual active units, not starts, exposure-years, retention, or completed courses; dividing by 2.5 is an analyst unit-alignment approximation.
The Memphis preventable-mortality result was sparse, not prespecified, and sensitive to small event-count changes; all-cause mortality was not significant.
The modern South Carolina age-two primary composite was null, and the ED finding did not survive multiplicity adjustment.
The 9-QALY mortality bridge is an undiscounted analyst cap inside the age-20 window, not a trial QALY estimate.
Historical $8,580 and $14,728 delivery costs are not current San Francisco marginal prices.
Total net assets are not demonstrated liquid or unrestricted; restrictions, pledge timing, and liquidity are unavailable.
Bay 2.5% and SF 0.2% are unsourced round allocation priors built from mismatched capacity and served units, not observed local spending or reach.
The weighted result is favorable-tail-sensitive, and marginal health-producing funding room is unpriced and unverified.
excludedBenefits: Child First health and family benefits
Avoided Medicaid, emergency, child-welfare, education, and justice-system spending
Sibling, caregiver, and intergenerational spillovers beyond modeled child QALYs
Non-mortality maternal health, child development, school-readiness, and parenting benefits not captured by the per-course QALY prior
National policy, training, research, and implementation-learning spillovers
